findings.title: The first-run HTTP journey no longer supplies the required setup fields

evidence.detail: The first-run setup POST contains only username and password.
Setup now validates the complete registrationSchema before calling createFirstAdmin.
displayName and passwordConfirmation are required registration fields.
After setup validation fails, the fixture attempts login with the same not-yet-created account.

findings.trigger: Run COAST_HTTP_TEST_URL HTTP journeys against a fresh disposable Coast installation without an already seeded coast-browser-test user.
findings.impact: The advertised first-run journey cannot establish its initial cookie, and subsequent tracking/page tests fail downstream. An existing account can hide the stale setup contract, so the fallback weakens first-run coverage.
findings.recommendation: Add displayName and matching passwordConfirmation to the setup payload, and keep login credentials as a separate payload. Make fresh bootstrap and existing-installation login expectations explicit so validation failure cannot masquerade as successful first-run coverage.
findings.verification: The current exact fixture object fails a harmless v.safeParse(registrationSchema, fixture) check for both missing fields. After repair, run the HTTP journey against a fresh disposable server/database and verify setup itself supplies the session cookie before later tests.

findings.title: Two database assertions still encode the previous Search/taste contracts

evidence.detail: Requires the other user's unavailable shared show to be absent, relying on old cutoff ordering rather than the unified catalogue contract.
Authenticated search ranks SQL relevance before UUID, rather than metadata updatedAt; it does not hide shared unavailable metadata.
Expects exactly four user_taste_profiles.
Creates movie/show/game/music/book/comic profiles, including empty profiles.

findings.trigger: Run the existing disposable database suite on the current working tree.
findings.impact: The parent audit's full DB run reports these two failures. The Search assertion does not demonstrate a source/privacy leak; the meaningful !available assertion follows it. The taste count assertion prevents the same test reaching its stale-cache ranking assertions.
findings.recommendation: Assert no availability/source grant for the other viewer rather than arbitrary absence from shared metadata results. Update taste expectations to the six supported profile media (prefer explicit medium identities) and retain later score/revision/privacy checks.
findings.verification: Parent-run log /private/tmp/coast-core-full-db.log reports failures at domain-application-db.test.ts:1024 and taste-cache-db.test.ts:22 (4 expected, 6 actual). Rerun both suites with disposable DB after test updates. This section did not run DB tests itself.

findings.title: Creating a playlist with an initial reading work bypasses its membership rule

evidence.detail: createList validates only that the initial work exists and inserts it directly at line 46.
addListItem checks the work category and rejects books/comics in playback playlists.
POST /lists passes the create payload to createList, exposing the inconsistent initial-member path.

findings.trigger: POST /api/v1/lists with {name:Reading playlist,playlist:true,mediaId:BOOK_OR_COMIC_UUID}.
findings.impact: Creation succeeds with a member that the ordinary Add path forbids. Playback expansion ignores that reading member, producing a visible playlist item with no valid playback entry. This is a validation consistency issue, not a cross-user authorization bypass.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same category rule when creating a playlist with an initial member. Share the small existing validation if useful; preserve atomic create-with-initial-item behavior.
findings.verification: Add a disposable DB regression asserting book/comic initial playlist creation fails without leaving a list, while ordinary reading lists and screen/audio playlist initial members still succeed.

findings.title: Taste-outbox uniqueness index targets runtime-unused jobs table

evidence.detail: Separate jobs declaration has no discovered production read/write caller;JSONB codec test inserts it.
outbox_taste_one_active_idx is attached to jobs rather than outboxActions.
Applied SQL creates named unique index ON jobs.
Real taste scheduling inserts outbox_actions;manual admission uses advisory lock at34.
Documentation incorrectly attributes active taste-job admission to a partial unique index.

findings.trigger: Maintaining the documented taste-job invariant or inspecting the named index as assurance of outbox deduplication.
findings.impact: The advertised database invariant does not constrain actual job rows;parallel unused schema obscures ownership. Existing locked scheduling means ordinary duplicate execution is not established.
findings.recommendation: Move the intended index to actual outbox via new migration and align schema,or explicitly document advisory-lock-only admission and remove misleading dead constraint. Review unused jobs table and codec test together before removal;do not create a second runtime.
findings.verification: Inspect index relation/predicate on disposable migrated DB and test intended active taste-job invariant on outbox_actions including terminal-state transitions;retain scheduler lock tests.

findings.title: Normal canonical music links discard stored artist navigation

evidence.detail: Artist and album-artist credits are persisted with separate roles and instance-scoped artist identities.
Persisted album/track cards route users to the canonical music page.
Canonical toItem explicitly returns artists:[] and albumArtists:[] without reading persisted credits.
The route supplies connectionId:'' to the shared presenter.
Artist links are built only from those role-specific artist arrays, so canonical pages lose all artist destinations.

findings.trigger: Browse an album/track with valid artist credits and follow its ordinary musicCard link after musicLibrary persists it.
findings.impact: Provider detail routes preserve album-artist versus performer navigation, but the default canonical detail path always drops it. An album with only album-artist credits may also lose its visible subtitle because persistence falls back to performing artists, not album artists.
findings.recommendation: Hydrate persisted role-specific music credits in the canonical read model and map navigable artist links through the viewer's enabled owned connection for that artist instance. Preserve plain credit text when no permitted source exists, using the established shared presenter and interface.
findings.verification: Disposable loader fixture: persist an album with only albumArtists and a track with distinct performers, follow musicCard.href, and assert expected subtitle/credit roles and authorised artist links. Disconnect the source and assert credit text remains without generating /music/work/{providerArtistId} links.

findings.title: Removing an IGDB parent does not remove the old verified variant link

evidence.detail: Explicit details refresh requests the expanded fields including parent_game/version_parent; this finding concerns a successful full response, not an incremental observation.
A current parsed response without parent_game/version_parent maps parent to undefined.
Import upserts a variant only when a parent exists; no corresponding deletion handles an authoritative parent removal.
Presentation continues borrowing the old parent's fields from the surviving row.
Taste metadata also keeps selecting features from that surviving parent row.

findings.trigger: Use the game's explicit Refresh metadata action (games/import -> igdbDetails) after importing a verified parent, and return a successful full expanded IGDB response for that identity with the parent relation removed.
findings.impact: The local game indefinitely borrows artwork/overview and taste features from a parent that the current provider response no longer verifies. A successful refresh cannot return the game to independent presentation.
findings.recommendation: Within the same metadata import transaction, remove the existing variant relation owned by this provider when the authoritative full response has no distinct parent. Keep the game UUID, Steam ownership and private tracking intact.
findings.verification: Extend the existing verified variant DB fixture: import child+parent, reimport the same child with no parent, assert the variant row disappears and gameDetails/workTasteFeatures use the child's own metadata; also test changing to a different verified parent.

findings.title: Dense compound source has no consistent authoring guard

evidence.detail: Queue eligibility is a large compound expression; 61 modules have multiple >240-character source lines.
Verification scripts cover types/build/tests/inventory but no formatting/lint convention.

findings.trigger: Reviewing or modifying control flow and multi-branch queries across feature implementations
findings.impact: Harder local reasoning and diffs; no runtime failure claimed from formatting alone
findings.recommendation: Agree one convention and separate formatting from behavior changes; extract only concrete shared responsibilities
findings.verification: Formatting-only diff and existing behavioral checks

findings.title: Reader engines depend on their dispatcher for a shared cancellation helper

evidence.detail: Shared cancellation helper and lazy format dispatcher are colocated.
PDF engine imports the dispatcher at runtime for readerLoad.
EPUB engine imports the same dispatcher while dispatcher imports EPUB dynamically.

findings.trigger: Isolating renderer code for tooling/testing or evolving engine loading
findings.impact: Avoidable runtime dependency group; no eager-loading/initialization defect asserted
findings.recommendation: Move only cancellation helper into an adjacent pure module, preserving lazy dispatch and type contracts
findings.verification: Reader close/abort tests and selected-format lazy chunk checks

findings.title: The design guide contradicts the current mobile navigation and material inventory

evidence.detail: States primary navigation uses text-only pills on desktop and mobile.
Below 640px the actual Header hides text labels and displays navigation icons.
Names six shared treatments and says the six recipes are preserved.
Actual supported material variants are four: clear, glassLight, glassDark and glassProminent, each with a paired fallback.

findings.trigger: A maintainer follows the current source-of-truth design guide while changing shared navigation or material usage.
findings.impact: The guide can prompt an accidental restoration of obsolete mobile navigation or invalid material names, conflicting with the requirement to preserve approved UX. Passing token/fixture tests do not resolve which visual contract the documentation intends.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two guide statements with the approved current UI and actual four-variant API; record approval status accurately. Do not change mobile visuals or reintroduce recipes solely to make the older prose true.
findings.verification: Review the current narrow Header and Materials reference against the approved UI, then check that documented variant names match keyof glassPresets.materials and that mobile prose matches the resulting approved behavior.
